deities: Lord Ganesha - 600-year-old standing (khade) murti, rare straight-trunk form

history.dynasty: Hada Rajputs (traditional); temple patronized by the Kota royal family (the royal family reportedly revered the deity as kuldevta - weakly sourced, verify)
history.period: ~600 years old, i.e. ~15th century (traditional; exact date undocumented - verify)
history.summary: One of Kota's most famous temples, on the banks of the Chambal River. Its distinction is the ~600-year-old idol of Lord Ganesha in a standing (khade) posture with a straight trunk - described by sources as the only standing-Ganesha temple in Rajasthan (some say in India; verify). Accounts of discovery vary: one says a local king found the standing idol near the Chambal banks and built the temple; another says a cowherd noticed his cow offering milk at the spot, digging revealed the idol, and it was regarded as swayambhu (self-manifested) - flag both as tradition only. The temple is open on all sides except the sanctum; the ceiling reportedly has innumerable bells of different sizes that sound in the wind (verify). A large Shiva murti also stands in the complex, and a pond/lake behind the temple - which fills in the monsoon (the temple has been closed when water reached it, e.g. around 1995) - attracts peacocks and makes it a picnic spot. Ganesh Udyan (garden) lies nearby. Coordinates are from map geocode of the temple (address area Retwali, SH-33, Kota).

name: Khade Ganesh Ji Temple
town_description: Kota is a major city on the Chambal River in southeastern Rajasthan, best known nationally as India's coaching-education hub. On the Chambal's banks it also holds a string of old temples - Khade Ganesh Ji, the Mathuradheesh Temple of the old city, and the ancient Kansua Shiv Mandir - set around riverside gardens, the Chambal Garden and the old Patanpole quarter.

travel.railway: Kota Junction - major Delhi-Mumbai line station (verify distance to temple).
travel.road: On the banks of the Chambal River near Ganesh Nagar; one source places it about 14 km from the city centre (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ganesh Chaturthi (September) for the annual fair - crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily per one travel source (verify - confirm locally). Best visited early morning; coaching students visit for blessings before exams.
